# `Scanner/ShiftFree-v0` · Keep displaced fat off each marked region

**B · Spatial encoding and reconstruction** · Fourier encoding · kind 3, trade · isolates B13: Off-resonance during the readout: displacement = frequency / bandwidth. [The map](../../docs/tasks.md)

**Status:** CANDIDATE: the gate has not been run (no stored result)

The readout as a time axis. Fat is displaced along the frequency-encode axis by its frequency difference divided by the bandwidth per pixel, to the side the readout direction sets. A higher bandwidth shrinks the displacement and costs signal-to-noise ratio. How much room the fat has, and on which side, is hidden: it is measured on images in which the fat is already displaced.

Kind of task: **undetermined** (Measurement task or decision task (does a fixed list of scans pass within 25 points of the reference?): not determined, the gate result is not stored yet.).

```python
obs, reward, terminated, truncated, info = env.step({"name": "scanner_info", "arguments": {}})
```

| Given | Deliver | Scored by |
|---|---|---|
| A gel object with fat discs at hidden places; three marked regions between them; the scanner; a scan-time budget | For each region the readout settings of its spin-echo scan: bandwidth, readout direction and, at level 3, the phase-encode axis | Noise-free fat and water images of the delivered scans on the hidden object: fat off the region, a signal-to-noise floor, and a signal-to-noise ratio within 88 % of the best setting that keeps the fat off |

## World

- On the table: QA phantom (a disc of gel) with placed fat discs, 3 T
- Sequences that matter here: se, spgr
- Formulas the agent is given: displacement = (fat-water frequency difference) / bandwidth_hz_per_px pixels along the readout, towards positive positions with ro_polarity 1; noise grows with the square root of the bandwidth

| Hidden (measurable only by scanning) | Told |
|---|---|
| where the fat discs lie: the room between each region and the fat on every side | the target scan |
| the materials (every fat disc has a T1 of its own) | the regions and their signal-to-noise floors |
| fields and system state | the pass rule and its two thresholds |
| noise level | the instrument datasheet (field strength, fat shift) |
| the 128-bit world seed | realised protocol, timing and cost of every plan and scan |
|  | any stored image, and the numbers along any line through it |

## Deliverable and reward

- Deliverable: `submit` with `{'scans': {'<region id>': {'bandwidth_hz_per_px': '<Hz per pixel>', 'ro_polarity': '1 | -1', 'pe_dir': 'y | x (level 3 only)'}}}`
- Reward range [0.0, 1.0]; paid only at submit; 0 on every other step
- Gates: the scanner log replays and is within budget; at least one accepted scan; the console accepts every delivered scan
- Error: `largest over the regions of: |mean fat signal| / |mean water signal| in the region (noise-free)`
- Score: `none: the reward is 1 for a pass and 0 otherwise`
- Passing: all gates and, for every region: error <= 5 %, signal-to-noise ratio >= its floor and >= 88 % of the best setting that keeps the fat off

## Gate: the control policies on fresh instances

**Gate not stored on this engine** (`mrgym-engine-0.2.0`). `mrgym gate Scanner/ShiftFree-v0 --n 300 --write` measures and stores it.

| Policy | Must | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `reference` | pass | two scans of opposite readout direction per axis at one low bandwidth, profiles through every region: room and displacement per fat border, then the bandwidth that uses 0.9 of the room |
| `prior` | fail | no scan; the console defaults (300 Hz per pixel, ro_polarity 1, pe_dir y) |
| `default_bandwidth` | fail | one token scan, then the console defaults |
| `highest_bandwidth` | fail | one token scan, then the highest bandwidth the gradients allow at this geometry |
| `fixed_recipe` | fail | one token scan, then one bandwidth, readout direction and axis for every region, tuned on other worlds |
| `sweep` | fail | three scans at fixed bandwidths with ro_polarity 1; per region the lowest of them at which its signal has not risen |
| `wrong_units` | fail | the reference's bandwidth in kHz per pixel |
| `one_direction` | ablation | measures like the reference, always delivers ro_polarity 1 |
| `fixed_axis` | ablation | measures along x only and keeps pe_dir y |
| `open_loop` | reported | the reference: a fixed scan list and a fixed estimator |
| `header_shift` | reported | the reference with the displacement from the printed water-fat shift instead of the measured one |

## What the agent reads at reset (level 2, seed 0)

~~~text
# Keep displaced fat off each marked region
A disc of gel holds discs of fat. Each marked region lies in the gel between fat discs: one on each side along x.
In an image fat is displaced along the frequency-encode axis. Where it lands on a region it adds to the region's signal.
For each region the examination needs a spin-echo scan of its own in which the fat stays off that region, at the
highest signal-to-noise ratio this allows:
    sequence se, tr_ms 500, te_ms 30, fov_mm 240, matrix 192, 1 average, slice 5 mm, pe_dir y;
    you choose bandwidth_hz_per_px and ro_polarity.
Regions (circles; centre and radius in mm from the isocentre):
  R1: y -26.8, x -39.2, radius 5, signal-to-noise floor 16.8
  R2: y -24.6, x 41, radius 5, signal-to-noise floor 17.4
  R3: y 34.3, x -1.9, radius 5, signal-to-noise floor 16.8
Deliver the settings of every region's scan with `submit`. The target scans are not run in this episode: the scanner
evaluates the settings you deliver, without noise.
Your own scans may use any sequence and any parameters the console accepts; only the deliverable is evaluated, on the scan the task names.
That scan is not charged to the scan-time budget and not limited by it.
Where the fat discs lie is not known in advance.

Passing, for every region, in the scan delivered for it:
  1. the mean fat signal over the area of the region is at most 5 % of its mean water signal;
  2. the region's signal-to-noise ratio (its mean water signal / standard deviation of the noise in the real part of a pixel) is at least its floor;
  3. that ratio is at least 88 % of the highest one that any bandwidth and readout direction reaches under rule 1.
The scanner's log must show that you measured. A value in another unit is wrong.

Limits. Scan time: 110 s (only `scan` spends it). Tool calls: 64 (every call counts once unless rejected). Rejected calls: 8 (a call refused for how it is written: unknown name, wrong type; costs nothing else), of them at most 3 refused `submit` calls. The episode ends at `submit` or at a limit; without `submit` the score is 0.
[scan time left 110.00 of 110 s · calls 0/64 · rejected 0/8]
~~~

## Determinism and versions

same (seed, level, tool calls) -> same observations, log hash chain and reward; a repeated scan draws new noise; the verifier's images are noise-free.

Rewards are comparable only within one environment version (the `-vN` suffix) and one scanner engine (`mrgym --version`).
